title: Boundary lifting for local equivalences of hypercover-local simplicial presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Let $H$ be a small dense set of these hypercovers. Give $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ the projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations, and its left Bousfield localization $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H$ at the augmentation maps $U_\bullet\to h_T$ in $H$ [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison]. In this localization cofibrations are the projective cofibrations, fibrant objects are the projectively fibrant $H$-local objects, and $H$-local means that every augmentation in $H$ induces an equivalence of projectively derived mapping spaces into that object. Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A Kan complex is a simplicial set with fillers for all horns. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the simplicial set represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces, and a horn is the union of all faces except one. For objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves, a local weak equivalence means an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, vertex $x\in X(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of the homotopy groups $\pi_m(X|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(Y|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. Here $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced covering-sieve topology.

If $p:X\to Y$ is a fibration in $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H$, both $X$ and $Y$ are fibrant there, and $p$ is a local weak equivalence, then $p$ is an objectwise trivial Kan fibration. More explicitly, for every $T\in\mathcal C$ and $n\ge0$, every commutative square with left map $h_T\times\partial\Delta^n\to h_T\times\Delta^n$ and right map $p$ has a diagonal lift.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Lemma 6.4 and the projective-model paragraph in the proof of Theorem 6.2, pp. 17-18 (published numbering Lemma 6.5, as cited by Choudhury--Gallauer Lemma 5.13).

proof.text: Use the existing projective model, which is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial. The given localization at $H$ can also be taken simplicial: for each $U\to h_S$ in $H$, choose a projective cofibrant replacement $QU\to U$, and factor $QU\to h_S$ as a cofibration $QU\to B_U$ followed by a projective trivial fibration $B_U\to h_S$. Both $QU$ and $B_U$ are cofibrant. Apply the simplicial Bousfield-model theorem to the small set of these cofibrations. The derived mapping-space theorem shows that locality for $QU\to B_U$ is exactly locality for $U\to h_S$: the replacement arrows are objectwise weak equivalences and hence become equivalences in the projective localization. Thus this model has the same local objects and the same derived mapping-space weak equivalences as the stipulated $H$-localization. Its cofibrations also agree, so its fibrations agree, being the maps lifting all trivial cofibrations. We may use its unchanged simplicial enrichment, tensors and cotensors.

source.place: Section 2, printed p. 6, and projective-model paragraph of Theorem 6.2, printed p. 18; cofibrant-map presentation of the localization expanded using the cited generic model theorems.

proof.text: Every objectwise weak equivalence is an $H$-equivalence, since projectively derived mapping spaces carry it to equivalences. Therefore each projective trivial cofibration is a trivial cofibration in the localized model. The assumed localized fibration $p$ lifts these maps and is consequently a projective fibration, hence an objectwise Kan fibration. The given localized fibrancy of $X,Y$ makes them objectwise Kan. In particular $p$ is a local Kan fibration: each horn square already has a filler over its original representable, so the maximal covering sieve suffices. Its local weak-equivalence hypothesis is exactly the homotopy-sheaf hypothesis of the relative-lifting primitive.

source.place: Lemma 6.4, first paragraph of proof, printed p. 17; the projective case uses the Quillen identity comparison instead of injective fibrations.

proof.text: Fix $T\in\mathcal C$, $n\ge0$, and a boundary square; put $K=\partial\Delta^n$ and $L=\Delta^n$. The constant augmented simplicial presheaf $h_T\to h_T$ is a hypercover: every augmented matching map is an identity. Apply the strict relative-lifting primitive to this hypercover and to $p$ with the two properties established in step 2. Both $K,L$ have finitely many nondegenerate simplices, also when $n=0$ and $K$ is empty. It gives a hypercover $U\to h_T$ and an actual lift $L\times U\to X$ of the restricted square. By the assumed density of $H$, choose $v:V\to U$ with $V\to h_T$ in $H$; precomposing the lift with $1_L\times v:L\times V\to L\times U$ preserves both strict triangle equations. Rename this $H$-hypercover $U$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1 and proof, printed pp. 13-14; Lemma 6.4, printed pp. 17-18, identity hypercover and density refinement.

proof.text: Work in the simplicial localized model of step 1. Define the cotensor objects $A=X^L$, $B=Y^L\times_{Y^K}X^K$ and $r:A\to B$, where $r$ combines restriction along $K\hookrightarrow L$ with $p$. The simplicial pushout-product axiom implies that $r$ is a localized fibration: a lifting square against a trivial cofibration $j$ is adjoint to a square of $p$ against $j\mathbin\square(K\hookrightarrow L)$, a trivial cofibration. For $Z=X$ and for $Z=Y$, a square from a trivial cofibration $j$ to $Z^L\to *$ is adjoint to a square from $j\mathbin\square(\varnothing\hookrightarrow L)$ to the fibration $Z\to *$; the pushout product is trivial, so a lift exists. Thus both $A=X^L$ and $Y^L$ are fibrant. A square from $j$ to $X^K\to Y^K$ is adjoint to a square from $j\mathbin\square(\varnothing\hookrightarrow K)$ to $p$; this pushout product is also trivial, proving that $X^K\to Y^K$ is a fibration. Since $Y^L$ is fibrant, the pullback defining $B$ is fibrant: its map to $Y^L$ is a pullback of that fibration, and composition with $Y^L\to *$ is a fibration. Pullback and composition preserve this right lifting class by pulling back squares and then taking the two successive lifts.

source.place: Lemma 6.4, mapping-space diagram and simplicial-model axiom, printed p. 18; cotensor corner and its fibrancy expanded by tensor/cotensor adjunction.

proof.text: Choose a projective cofibrant replacement $q:QU\to U$ and write $e:QU\to U\to h_T$. The object $h_T$ is projectively cofibrant (its initial map is the degree-zero representable boundary generator), and so both $h_T$ and $QU$ are cofibrant in the localization. The augmentation $U\to h_T$ is inverted by definition of $H$-locality and $q$ is an objectwise weak equivalence; hence $e$ is an $H$-equivalence. Form the commuting square with rows $\operatorname{Map}(h_T,A)\to\operatorname{Map}(QU,A)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(h_T,B)\to\operatorname{Map}(QU,B)$ induced by $e$, and columns induced by $r$. Its four entries are Kan complexes and its vertical maps are Kan fibrations by the simplicial mapping axiom, using cofibrancy of the sources and step 4. Its rows are weak equivalences: enriched mapping spaces from these cofibrant sources to the localized fibrants $A,B$ represent localized derived mapping spaces, which send $e$ to an equivalence. The original boundary square gives a vertex $b$ of the lower-left space by cotensor adjunction. The strict lift of step 3, precomposed with $L\times q$, gives a vertex $a'$ of the upper-right space whose image is exactly the image of $b$ in the lower-right space. No cofibrancy of the hypercover $U$ has been assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.4 mapping-space square, printed p. 18, with the projective replacement required in the final paragraph of the proof of Theorem 6.2 on that page.

proof.text: The top row of this square is surjective on $\pi_0$, so there is a vertex $a$ in the upper-left space whose image has the component of $a'$. Commutativity shows that the images of $r(a)$ and $b$ lie in the same component of the lower-right space. Injectivity on $\pi_0$ of the bottom row therefore gives a finite edge path, allowing reversed edges, from $r(a)$ to $b$ in the lower-left space. Lift this path through the left vertical Kan fibration starting at $a$. Each edge, in either orientation, lifts because both endpoint inclusions $\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ are one-dimensional horns. The resulting vertex $\widetilde a$ lies over $b$. Under cotensor adjunction, $\widetilde a:h_T\to X^L$ is the required map $h_T\times L\to X$, and $r(\widetilde a)=b$ is exactly the pair of strict triangle equations for the original square.

source.place: Lemma 6.4, final paragraph of proof, printed p. 18; component and path-lifting argument written out.

proof.text: The boundary square was arbitrary. Evaluating the tensor--representable adjunction identifies its fillers with fillers for every $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ against $p(T):X(T)\to Y(T)$: explicitly a natural map $h_T\times M\to Z$ is determined by its value on $\mathrm{id}_T$, an $M\to Z(T)$ map, and the inverse sends $(a:V\to T,m)$ to the restriction of that value along $a$. The Kan-model boundary criterion now makes every $p(T)$ a trivial Kan fibration, equivalently a Kan fibration and weak homotopy equivalence. The generator with $n=0$ uses the empty boundary and proves surjectivity on vertices as well. This is the full objectwise conclusion.

tool_uses.why: Generic projective presheaf model gives generators, projective cofibrant replacements and objectwise fibrations; the compact-support unit has no separate model-category construction.
Generic simplicial Bousfield existence theorem, applied only to cofibrations between cofibrant objects after replacement, supplies the simplicial localization.
Generic derived mapping-space definition of localization supplies its local equivalences; no identification with homotopy-sheaf equivalences is used.
Generic model factorizations, simplicial mapping axiom and enriched/derived mapping-space comparison justify replacements and the mapping square.
Only its explicit simplicial pushout-product and weak-factorization definitions are used to prove the cotensor-corner facts directly; none of its coherent diagram comparison theorem is needed.
Generic Kan model definitions and boundary criterion supply edge-path lifting and identify the final sectionwise trivial fibration.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q123-3562d98eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I could not read the DHI paper (arXiv:math/0205027v2) at the cited places: it is not in literature/, I found no copy on the machine, and network access is blocked for reviewers. So I checked every step against the full statements of the nodes it cites, and checked the new node's statement mathematically. The delivery's WANTED line stands. Statement: the item is unchanged and not a target node, so no base-change or coefficient check applies. No SGA is cited. Step 1: QU->B_U makes both ends cofibrant, as the Bousfield theorem requires. T-local equals H-local and T-equivalences equal W_H, and the cofibrations agree, so the fibrations agree. Step 2: objectwise weak equivalences lie in W_H, so p is a projective fibration and X, Y are objectwise Kan. Step 3: the constant h_T->h_T is a hypercover with identity matching maps, K is empty when n=0, and density keeps the strict equations. Step 4: the pushout-product adjunction makes the corner r a fibration and X^L, Y^L and B fibrant. Step 5: h_T is cofibrant (the n=0 generator), e is in W_H, the rows are weak equivalences into localized fibrants, the columns are Kan fibrations, and a' maps exactly to e*(b). Step 6: pi_0 surjectivity and injectivity give an edge path, and lifting it through the endpoint horns gives a vertex exactly over b. Step 7: the Yoneda adjunction and the boundary criterion (including n=0) finish the proof. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. New node lem-cbc-hypercover-relative-lifting: true by DHI Prop 5.1 plus Jardine's local-fibration comparison. It is self-contained, statement-only, searched in Mathlib, has its blueprint fields, and is strictly smaller than the item (no D1). I tested K=L, K=L=empty, K=empty with L=Delta^0, the trivial topology and empty covers. Splitter note: if DHI 5.1 assumes boundary-lifting local acyclicity, the comparison from homotopy-sheaf local weak equivalences to that hypothesis needs its own node when this node is split. rg found no duplicate: kan-relative-realization-lift, dense-hypercover-set, bousfield-quillen-descent and the scheme refinement nodes all differ, and there is no cycle. All six off-unit generic model tool_uses are accepted. No fixes.
